context.title: Two Sons, One Throne
context.summary: As David lies old and weak, his son Adonijah declares himself king, but Nathan and Bathsheba remind David of his promise, and Solomon is anointed instead.
context.background: Israel had no fixed rule of succession. Adonijah, David's eldest surviving son (2 Samuel 3:4), had the support of the army commander Joab and the priest Abiathar. Solomon had the prophet Nathan, the priest Zadok, and Benaiah's royal guard.

customs.note: Putting Solomon on David's own mule was a public sign that the old king had chosen him as heir.
Altars had horn-shaped corners. Clinging to them was a plea for sanctuary.

watchFor: Two rival celebrations happen at once, at En-rogel and at the Gihon spring (vv. 9, 33).
Nathan and Bathsheba repeat each other's words to remind David of his oath (vv. 13–27).

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Abishag
people.summary: Father of (i.e., “given to”) error, a young woman of Shunem, distinguished for her beauty. She was chosen to minister to David in his old age.

people.name: Adonijah
people.summary: The fourth son of David (2 Sam. 3:4). After the death of his elder brothers, Amnon and Absalom, he became heir-apparent to the throne. But Solomon, a younger brother, was preferred to him.

people.name: Haggith
people.summary: Festive; the dancer, a wife of David and the mother of Adonijah (2 Sam. 3:4; 1 Kings 1:5, 11; 2:13; 1 Chr. 3:2), who, like Absalom, was famed for his beauty.

people.name: Absalom
people.summary: Father of peace; i.e., “peaceful” David’s son by Maacah (2 Sam. 3:3; comp. 1 Kings 1:6). He was noted for his personal beauty and for the extra-ordinary profusion of the hair of his head (2 Sam. 14:25,26).

people.name: Joab
people.summary: One of the three sons of Zeruiah, David’s sister, and “captain of the host” during the whole of David’s reign (2 Sam. 2:13; 10:7; 11:1; 1 Kings 11:15).

people.name: Abiathar
people.summary: Father of abundance, or my father excels, the son of Ahimelech the high priest. He was the tenth high priest, and the fourth in descent from Eli.

people.name: Zeruiah
people.summary: Stricken of the Lord, David’s sister, and the mother of Abishai, Joab, and Asahel (1 Chr. 2:16), who were the three leading heroes of David’s army, and being his nephews, they were admitted to the closest companionship with him.

people.name: Zadok
people.summary: A son of Ahitub, of the line of Eleazer (2 Sam. 8:17; 1 Chr. 24:3), high priest in the time of David (2 Sam. 20:25) and Solomon (1 Kings 4:4).

people.name: Nathan
people.summary: A prophet in the reigns of David and Solomon (2 Chr. 9:29). He is first spoken of in connection with the arrangements David made for the building of the temple (2 Sam. 7:2, 3, 17), and next appears as the reprover of David on account of his sin with Bathsheba (12:1-14).

people.name: Benaiah
people.summary: The son of Jehoiada, chief priest (1 Chr. 27:5). He was set by David over his body-guard of Cherethites and Pelethites (2 Sam. 8:18; 1 Kings 1:32; 1 Chr. 18:17).

people.name: Jehoiada
people.summary: The father of Benaiah, who was one of David’s chief warriors (2 Sam. 8:18; 20:23).

people.name: Shimei
people.summary: One of David’s mighty men who refused to acknowledge Adonijah as David’s successor (1 Kings 1:8).

people.name: Rei
people.summary: Friendly, one who maintained true allegiance to king David (1 Kings 1:8) when Adonijah rebelled.

people.name: Judah
people.summary: Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah.

people.name: Solomon
people.summary: Peaceful, (Heb. Shelomoh), David’s second son by Bathsheba, i.e., the first after their legal marriage (2 Sam. 12). He was probably born about B.C. 1035 (1 Chr. 22:5; 29:1).

people.name: Bathsheba
people.summary: Daughter of the oath, or of seven, called also Bath-shu’a (1 Chr. 3:5), was the daughter of Eliam (2 Sam. 11:3) or Ammiel (1 Chr. 3:5), and wife of Uriah the Hittite.

people.name: Jonathan
people.summary: Son of the high priest Abiathar, and one who adhered to David at the time of Absalom’s rebellion (2 Sam. 15:27, 36).

places.name: En-rogel
places.summary: Fountain of the treaders; i.e., “foot-fountain;” also called the “fullers’ fountain,” because fullers here trod the clothes in water. It has been identified with the “fountain of the virgin”, the modern ‘Ain Ummel-Daraj.

places.name: Serpent's Stone
places.summary: The serpent-stone, a rocky plateau near the centre of the village of Siloam, and near the fountain of En-rogel, to which the women of the village resort for water (1 Kings 1:5-9).

places.name: Gihon
places.summary: The only natural spring of water in or near Jerusalem is the “Fountain of the Virgin”, which rises outside the city walls on the west bank of the Kidron valley.
